paragraphs: The Vario 616D has been part of the Vario range since 1996, and across its single generation has used two different engines — from the OM612 through to the later OM647. These are the heavier-chassis variants of the Vario, using 2.2L to 2.7L diesel units shared with the equivalent-era Sprinter. They're known for the same timing chain and injector seal wear pattern as the lighter-chassis Varios, a well-documented specialist pattern. The Vario 616D is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every VARIO 616D on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the VARIO 616D from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the Vario 616D uses two distinct engines, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an OM612 part will work on an OM647 van — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (OM612 or OM647) via registration or VIN - Your van's chassis variant and weight rating - Ancillary specification and any fitment considerations

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Vario quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
